claims.text: Controlled low-temperature annealing can promote nanoscale precipitation in magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Annealing-induced nanoscale precipitates will increase the coercive field by creating additional domain-wall pinning sites.
The initial as-cast alloy has a relatively homogeneous, single-phase microstructure.
A sub-recrystallization anneal can induce nanoscale precipitates without causing full recrystallization or unwanted phase transformations.
An inert atmosphere will prevent oxidation during annealing.
Holding below the alloy's recrystallization threshold for a suitable duration can nucleate fine precipitates without coarsening them.
The proposed treatment is applicable to magnetic high-entropy alloys having moderate compositional complexity.
The anneal will form fine nanoscale precipitates dispersed throughout the matrix.
Fine nanoscale precipitates act as pinning centers that inhibit magnetic domain-wall motion.
Precipitate-mediated domain-wall pinning requires a higher applied field to reverse magnetization.
The annealed alloy will have a higher coercive field than the matched as-cast alloy.
The as-cast baseline has minimal intrinsic domain-wall pinning.
The coercivity increase depends on forming nanoscale precipitates without extensive grain growth or unwanted secondary phases.
Alternative phase transformations or excessive precipitate coarsening may prevent the coercivity increase.
The precipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction required to maximize pinning are uncertain.
The magnitude or occurrence of the effect may depend on alloy composition.
